title: BLOCK DATA — the only way to initialise COMMON-block variables in F77
sourceContent:
BLOCK DATA SETUP_TABLES
C     A BLOCK DATA program unit is the ONLY F77 construct that can
C     initialise COMMON-block variables via DATA. Trying to put the
C     DATA inside a SUBROUTINE that declares the same COMMON is a
C     compile error. Java/C# rewrites usually fold this into a
C     static initializer -- but the BLOCK DATA must be REFERENCED
C     somewhere (via EXTERNAL) or the linker drops it.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL THRESHOLDS(3)
      COMMON /CFG/ THRESHOLDS
      DATA THRESHOLDS / 0.1, 0.5, 0.9 /
      END
notes: BLOCK DATA is a unique-to-Fortran construct. The legacy idiom is to put all configuration constants in one BLOCK DATA file. Rewriting to a Java 'static final' class works, but the spec must capture: (a) the table values themselves, (b) the fact they're meant to be visible globally, (c) that the rewrite needs to ensure the initialiser actually runs (the linker drop bug).
